title: Michigan certification curriculum and research coverage
purpose: Evidence checklist and training-coverage catalog for human review; no AI food-safety or legal clearance.
scopeBasis: All 20 entries in the current MAMI study-guide index, expanded only to taxa explicitly named or separately marked as related/unresolved. The index is not treated as an exhaustive statutory whitelist.

statusDefinitions.documented_named_targets: Primary names on a current MAMI guide linked from its curriculum index; human scope and individual specimen inspection remain required.
statusDefinitions.documented_group_exact_species_unresolve: Curriculum group is explicit but an exhaustive modern species list is absent.
statusDefinitions.research_only_outside_documented_curricu: Useful research category; no certification coverage established from reviewed index.
statusDefinitions.related_taxa: Discussion, comparison or lookalike evidence only; never promoted automatically to covered targets.

certificationScopes.label: Full wild-mushroom certification
certificationScopes.scopeBasis: 20 indexed study-guide entries, with named targets, form restrictions and unresolved group boundaries recorded here.

certificationScopes.label: Morel-only certification
certificationScopes.scopeBasis: Morels only; does not extend to other curriculum groups.

salesRules.summary: Each wild mushroom offered for sale requires inspection and a safety determination by a currently approved/certified mushroom identification expert within their actual scope.
A seller may be certified or arrange inspection by a certified expert. Stores and restaurants must obtain mushrooms through an approved source.
The inspecting expert must be able to show current certification; scope and expiry need human verification.

Section 3-201.16(B) names regulated cultivation operations and packaged products of regulated processing plants as exceptions to that section. These are not generic exemptions for a forager or an AI result.
Retail bulk containers need scientific and common names. Wholesale bulk labeling has specific packaged-label or written-agreement provisions.
Packaged product labels require the common name and applicable ingredient, net-weight, producer/address and allergen information; cottage-food labels have additional requirements.
Keep sale records for at least two years and make them available to MDARD.
salesRules.privacy: Collect transaction information only from the user; do not import public certification-register personal records.

salesRules.summary: Whole raw produce sales may not require a food-establishment license; processing, warehousing and sales activities can change applicable requirements.

Current MDARD guidance permits qualifying raw or dried mushrooms under cottage-food rules with proof of expert identification. Dehydration must satisfy the applicable home-kitchen, active-drying, labeling and direct-consumer conditions.
Michigan DNR states food foraged on state lands is for personal use, not resale; private-land foraging requires owner permission. Site-specific authority still applies.
A user-confirmed group or species label is research annotation. It is not automatically certified expert inspection, a safe-to-eat determination, or legal sales clearance.

reviewEvidenceChecklist: Whole specimen and multiple views, including underside and base
Substrate and associated tree recorded when relevant
Physical interior or spore evidence when required by the expert
Human identification, confidence, unresolved alternatives and reviewer role recorded separately from model guesses

sourceConflicts.issue: Older MAMI sales text states all slicing/drying needs a licensed kitchen; current MDARD guidance describes a conditional cottage-food route.
sourceConflicts.resolution: Use current regulator guidance for processing conditions; do not implement the older blanket prohibition.

sourceConflicts.issue: Current accessible curriculum pages retain older species names, spellings and open taxonomic questions.
sourceConflicts.resolution: Preserve source names and typed aliases; current taxon-database mappings need separate provenance and cannot widen certification scope.

researchGaps: No separate closed regulator-issued modern species whitelist was located in the reviewed primary materials.
MAMI does not publish an exhaustive current species list for every genus-level guide.
Taxonomic aliases, legacy names and Michigan occurrence require independent resolution before species-level model labels.
Observation-level photos cannot certify aborted form, full specimen identity, freshness or sales inspection.
Broad foraging groups are visual review categories, not evolutionary clades or edibility labels.
All model species outputs remain hypotheses until human review; certification eligibility remains a separate record.
